3

The document editor (document.html) writes and edits text documents like Word or LibreOffice Writer: paragraphs and headings, fonts and colours, alignment and spacing, bullet and numbered lists, tables, images, headers and footers, find and replace. The editing component is Univer Docs.

Files

Format Open Save Notes
Word (.docx) yes yes page size and margins, styles, headings, text formatting, lists, tables, images, hyperlinks, headers and footers with page numbers
OpenDocument (.odt, LibreOffice Writer) yes (also templates .ott) yes the same as for Word; footnotes and endnotes are placed at the end of the document
Word with macros (.docm), templates (.dotx) yes as .docx macros are not kept; a template becomes a new document
Text (.txt, .md) yes yes (.txt) only the text; formatting, tables and images are lost; a Markdown file opens as its text and is saved unchanged
Markdown (.md) as text yes headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, links, bullet, numbered and check lists, tables and images (embedded); no colours, fonts, alignment, page layout, headers and footers
Web page (.html) no yes text, formatting, lists, tables, images and links; no page layout
PDF no via 🖨 see Printing and PDF
  • Open (Ctrl+O) opens a file; you can also drop it onto the window. New starts an empty document.
  • Save (Ctrl+S) saves in the file's format: directly into the file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop, as a download in Firefox and on Android (replace the original file with it). Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S) asks for the name and the format.
  • The file name in the toolbar shows • while there are unsaved changes.

Printing and PDF

🖨 (Ctrl+P) prints the document with its page size and margins; choose Save as PDF (Chrome, Edge, Android) or Print to file (Firefox) as the printer to get a PDF. The header and footer of the document repeat on every page: in Chrome and Edge as text (pictures in them are left out) with the right page numbers, in Firefox with empty page numbers (Firefox cannot number pages there). The page breaks are made by the browser, so they can differ from the editor's pages; inserted page breaks are kept. Links stay clickable in the PDF, including the entries of a table of contents.

Documents from Word and LibreOffice are converted when they are opened; very complex layouts (text boxes, columns, tracked changes, comments) may look simpler. Keep the original file until you have checked the result. A "word" of more than 20,000 characters without a space (such as pasted base64 data) gets an invisible break point (U+200B) every 1,000 characters so that it can be shown; they are saved with the document.

Editing

The ribbon has the tabs Start (clipboard, bold/italic/underline/strike, sub- and superscript, paragraph style, size, font, colours, alignment, lists, checklists) and Insert (tables, images, links, horizontal line, emoji, symbols, header and footer, date and time). The usual shortcuts work: Ctrl+B/I/U, Ctrl+Z/Y, Ctrl+C/X/V, Ctrl+F to find. The status bar shows the word count and the zoom.

📐 Diagram in the toolbar opens an empty diagram in the diagram editor (a new window or tab); its first Save inserts the diagram as a picture at the cursor, later saves update it. When a diagram picture is selected (a click on it), 📐 Edit diagram opens it in the diagram editor again. An updated picture keeps its place and scale (at most the width of the text); Ctrl+Z undoes it. The diagram travels inside the picture (a PNG with the draw.io file), so it stays editable in the .docx file; Word shows the picture.

The language of the editing component follows the suite's language switch, and it follows the dark theme too.

Undo and redo are the first two buttons of the editor toolbar (also Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y).

Links

Select a text and press Ctrl+K (or Insert → 🔗, or 🔗 in the small toolbar above the selection) and enter the address: https://…, mailto:… or an e-mail address (it becomes a mailto: link); an address without a scheme gets https://. Pointing at (or tapping) a linked text shows the address with buttons to copy, edit or remove the link; Ctrl+K on a linked text changes it as well. Links are saved in Word, OpenDocument and HTML files and stay clickable in a PDF printed from the editor.

Table of contents and footnotes

📑 Contents inserts a table of contents at the paragraph of the cursor: the headings (paragraph styles Heading 1 to Heading 5), indented by level. After changing headings, click it again to update the table in place. In saved Word and OpenDocument files the entries are links to the headings (Ctrl+click in Word, click in LibreOffice); the table has no page numbers (the editor does not know them) – Word and LibreOffice can add a real index with page numbers if needed.

Comments

Select text and press Ctrl+Alt+M (or the comment button of the small toolbar above a selection) to comment on it; the first time, the editor asks for your name, which stands with your comments (change it in the settings: F1 → ⚙ Settings → Your name). The commented text is marked; 💬 Comments shows the comment panel: every comment with its replies, where you answer, edit or delete your own comments, mark a thread as resolved (✓) and filter by resolved or open threads. Clicking a comment selects its text.

Comments are kept in Word files (word/comments.xml; replies and the resolved state as Word 2013 and later writes them) and in OpenDocument files (office:annotation, with LibreOffice's replies and resolved state); comments of a Word or LibreOffice file show their authors. Web pages, Markdown, text files and printouts leave the comments out.

Spelling

ABC✓ (F7) opens the spelling panel beside the document (below it on a phone). It lists the unknown words of the document text (headers and footers are not checked); words with digits, words in capitals (abbreviations), web and mail addresses are skipped.

  • Click a word to select it in the document; click again to go to its next occurrence. The panel shows suggestions: a suggestion replaces all occurrences of the word.
  • Ignore skips the word until the editor is closed; Add to dictionary keeps it in the browser for good (for all dictionaries).
  • ↻ Check again after editing the text.

English (US) and German (Germany) are built in. For other languages, Load dictionary… takes a Hunspell dictionary: either the .aff and the .dic file together (for example from a LibreOffice installation), or a LibreOffice dictionary extension (.oxt, for example from extensions.libreoffice.org). Loaded dictionaries stay in the browser and are chosen in the list; 🗑 removes the selected one. The dictionary, the added words and the ignored words are the same as in the ABC selector in the header and in the other applications (see Spelling in the user guide); the panel works whether that selector is on or off, because the page of this editor is drawn as an image and cannot show underlines.

Footnotes and endnotes of Word and LibreOffice files are shown with their number in superscript; their texts are placed at the end of the document after a line, because the editor has no footnote area.

Symbols, emoji, date and time

Insert → Ω opens a picker of symbols (mathematics, Greek letters and common symbols), Insert → ☺ one of emoji with a search; a click inserts the character at the cursor. The suite's symbol picker (see the user guide) works here as well.

Insert → Date & time inserts today's date or the current time as text at the cursor: Date and Date (long) in the format of your region (e.g. 31/01/2026 and 31 January 2026, or 31.01.2026 and 31. Januar 2026), Date (ISO) as 2026-01-31, Time, or Date and time. It is ordinary text and does not change later; in headers and footers, the Header & Footer tab inserts a date that can be updated.

Page setup

The page setup button on the Start tab (at the right end, on a phone in the ⋮ menu) sets:

  • Layout: Pages like in Word, or No pages – continuous text without page edges (as text files open).
  • Paper size (A3, A4, A5, Letter, Legal or a custom width and height) and Orientation (portrait or landscape).
  • Margins at the top, bottom, left and right, in centimetres.

Apply changes the document (undo with Ctrl+Z). Page size, orientation and margins are kept in Word and OpenDocument files and are used for printing.

Headers, footers and page numbers

Headers and footers need a document with pages (one from Word or LibreOffice, or after choosing Pages in the page setup). Insert → Header & footer → Edit header or Edit footer (or a double-click into the top or bottom margin of a page) opens it for editing and shows the tab Header & Footer:

  • Page number → Current page or Total pages inserts the number at the cursor, e.g. "Page 3 of 12"; each page shows its own number. Date & time inserts the date or time. Refresh fields updates them.
  • Go to header / Go to footer switch between them; Different first page and Different odd and even pages give these pages their own header and footer; the distances of header and footer from the page edge are set at the right.
  • × (or Esc, or a double-click into the text) returns to the text.

On a phone, the buttons that do not fit are in the tab's ⋮ menu.

Page numbers are kept as page number fields in Word (PAGE, NUMPAGES) and OpenDocument files (text:page-number, text:page-count), so Word and LibreOffice number the pages too; page number fields of opened files work the same way. Other fields of Word and LibreOffice files keep the text they showed.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

On phones and tablets

Documents can be read and edited; the ribbon can be scrolled sideways. For longer texts a bigger screen and a keyboard are more comfortable.
